coverage_notes:
SOURCES USED. (1) Wikipedia 2023 Michigan Wolverines football team page — its roster-footer "Coaching staff"/"Support staff" block lists 24 people (head coach, 12 assistants, 11 support staff). This block is NOT in the article prose; it renders inside the roster template near the bottom of the page. (2) Touch the Banner, "2023 Michigan Football Staff" (Feb 17, 2023), the source Wikipedia itself cites — 36 people organized as ON FIELD / OFF FIELD / STRENGTH AND CONDITIONING / RECRUITING. This is the only source found that enumerates the graduate assistants, the assistant strength staff, and the recruiting/operations staff. (3) MGoBlue.com official release of Aug 24, 2023 ("Harbaugh Announces Coaching Duties for First Three Games of 2023"), used for Jim Harbaugh's full endowed title, Jack Harbaugh's assistant head coach title, and Ben Herbert's added associate head coach title. (4) Individual Wikipedia biographies used as corroboration for Fred Jackson, Bradford Banta, Mike Mallory, Rick Minter, and Connor Stalions.

QUOTE VERIFICATION. All 64 primary quotes plus 6 corroborating quotes were mechanically confirmed as exact substrings of the tag-stripped text of the live pages. Touch the Banner quotes take the visible-text form "Role: Name" because the page marks the role label with <strong> and the name follows in the same paragraph; a markdown-converting fetcher will render these as "**Role:** Name" instead, so match against plain text extraction. Trailing "*" (former Michigan player) and "#" (hired after the 2022 season) are part of the page text and are preserved inside the quotes.

TOTAL: 38 people. Union of Wikipedia (24) and Touch the Banner (36); Fred Jackson appears only in Wikipedia, and the 14 graduate assistants / assistant strength coaches / recruiting-operations staff appear only in Touch the Banner.

RING-RULE EXCLUSIONS (documented for the season but NOT on staff at the Jan 8, 2024 championship game). Chris Partridge, linebackers coach, separated from the program in mid-November 2023 — Wikipedia's parenthetical reads "fired Nov. 7", while contemporaneous reporting placed the separation on Nov. 17, 2023; I have flagged him but did not resolve the date discrepancy from a primary source. Connor Stalions, player personnel/defensive analyst, resigned in early November 2023 during the sign-stealing investigation. Both rows carry midseason_note. Rick Minter's row reflects that he took over as interim linebackers coach after Partridge's departure, so he was in that role at the championship game.

CONFLICT I COULD NOT FULLY RESOLVE. The Wayback capture of MGoBlue's official coaches directory (web.archive.org/web/20231118183709/https://mgoblue.com/sports/football/coaches, 12 names) lists Ron Bellamy as "Safeties Coach", Jay Harbaugh as "Tight Ends/Special Teams Coordinator", and Grant Newsome as "Tight Ends" — assignments that appear stale/garbled, since the school's own Aug. 24, 2023 release calls Jay Harbaugh "Special Teams Coordinator/Safeties Coach". I therefore used the Wikipedia/Touch the Banner assignments (Bellamy = wide receivers, Jay Harbaugh = special teams/safeties, Newsome = tight ends), which agree with each other and with the school's press release. I did not cite that archived directory as a source row because its name and title cells are split across separate table columns, so no contiguous verbatim "name + role" string exists on the page to quote.

GAPS — NOT DOCUMENTED, DELIBERATELY NOT PADDED. No medical (athletic trainers, team physicians), equipment, video, nutrition, academic-support, or football-operations-director personnel are included: Michigan did not publish a football support-staff directory, its athletics staff directory is a client-side JavaScript application whose data is absent from the archived HTML, and the Wayback CDX index surfaced no 2023 Michigan football media guide or information guide PDF. The weekly game-notes PDFs were located but MGoBlue served HTML rather than the PDF bytes and the Wayback copies did not resolve, so they could not be mined. Real staff in these categories certainly existed; I found no citable source for them, so the count of 38 should be read as a floor, not a complete roster.
